title_en: Chinese TV Dramas (5/20): Battles Inside the Palace
note_en: 表面上……，心里却…… sets what someone shows against what they really think: 表面上对对方彬彬有礼，心里却早已布好了下一步的计划 "on the surface she is polite to her rival, but in her heart she has long since planned her next move." Note that 却 ("but, yet") is an adverb: it comes after the subject or topic and right before the verb phrase, never at the start of the clause like English "but."

sentences.en: Over time, palace intrigue dramas have given rise to several classic character types that netizens have put names to, such as the "white lotus," who seems innocent and harmless but is actually a master schemer, and the "black lotus," who looks fragile but is ruthless and ends up defeating stronger rivals. These labels later came to be widely used to describe characters in other genres as well.

sentences.en: The costumes, makeup, and props in palace intrigue dramas usually follow the rank system of the Qing-dynasty harem closely: from the empress and the noble consort down to the pin and guiren ranks, each level differs in the color of its clothes, the elaborateness of its headdresses, and the grandeur of its living quarters. Some viewers have become so fascinated by the Qing harem hierarchy that they go and look up historical sources on it.

sentences.en: Many palace intrigue dramas also have the hallmarks of a shuang ju (a "satisfaction drama" built around payback): the heroine is often bullied at first and in a tough spot, but as the story unfolds she uses her wits to bring down her rivals one by one, and every time she turns the tables, viewers get a powerful emotional release and sense of satisfaction.

sentences.en: Some critics point out that although palace intrigue dramas center on female characters, their core conflict is usually still the competition for the emperor's favor, so the rivalry among women ultimately serves a male power structure. This makes some viewers feel that these shows actually offer a rather limited picture of women's independence and autonomy.
